question.problem: Estimate $2.1{e}^{0.2}$ using a differential $\text{d}f$ of the function $f(x,y)=x{e}^{y}$ at the point $(2,0).$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}x+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={e}^{y}\,\text{d}x+x{e}^{y}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

At the point $(2,0),$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & ={e}^{0}\,\text{d}x+2\cdot {e}^{0}\,\text{d}y \\  & =1\,\text{d}x+2\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

So, if we move to the point $(2+Δx,0+Δy),$ then we can approximate the change in $f$ as

$$
Δf≈1\,Δx+2\,Δy
$$

Note that 

$$
2.1{e}^{0.2}=f(2.1,0.2),
$$

so we want to move to the point $(2.1,0.2).$

Moving from $(2,0)$ to $(2.1,0.2),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δx & =2.1-2=0.1, \\ Δy & =0.2-0=0.2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δf & ≈1\cdot (0.1)+2\cdot (0.2) \\  & ≈0.1+0.4 \\  & ≈0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that the value of $f$ decreases by about $0.5.$ Consequently, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2.1,0.2) & ≈f(2,0)+0.5 \\ 2.1{e}^{0.2} & ≈2{e}^{0}+0.5 \\  & ≈2+0.5 \\  & ≈2.5.\end{aligned}
$$
